# Live rich-text cutover + state echo suppression + LWW conflict safety

## Context / Problem
This story **cuts the live Cloud and DC send paths over to the now-capable rich
codecs** (delivered by `e59d` and `271c`, on which this story depends) and makes
that cutover echo-safe. Because the DC codec is one-way and lossy, loop prevention
cannot rely on `decode(encode(x))==x`. Both clients must suppress echo by
**state**: compare the current Jira value against the last-synced baseline the
reconciler already keeps (ADR 0026, `binding_store.py:102`; `_BASELINE_FIELDS` at
`:108`; `set_baseline` at `:459`). We must also not silently destroy either side's
edits under concurrency, and any state we add must respect epic `0303`'s churn
discipline (a per-pass timestamp there caused the tickets-store bloat this feature
must not regress).

**Why the cutover lives HERE, not in the leaves.** `e59d`/`271c` deliver capable
codecs but deliberately leave the live send sites on the plain/identity path, so
that the observable format change and its echo-safety land **together** in one
story (this one), never a hazard-before-safety window.

## Prior art in this repo (build on the existing convergence, do NOT re-invent it)
- The rich-text COMPARE normalization already exists as the codec's
  **`normalize_outbound`** op (`RichTextCodec`, `adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py`).
  The description diff already routes every side through it / the equivalent
  `adf.normalize_description`: `OutboundFieldMapper.map_fields_to_remote`
  (`outbound_mapper.py:77`), `outbound_fields.py:564`, and `inbound_differ.py:210`
  (Jira side at `:212`). This story adds the three-way BASELINE layer ON TOP of
  that convergence; it does NOT add a second, parallel `norm()`.
- `binding_store.py` already persists the last-synced baseline (ADR 0026); this
  story extends that record, it does not create a new store.
- The codec law `normalize_outbound(t) == decode_inbound(to_wire(t))`
  (`test_rich_text_codec.py:163`) and the comment dedup that depends on it
  (`outbound_comments.py:48`) are preserved by routing every compare through the
  codec op.

## The live cutover (both clients — this story's new scope)
Reroute the direct plain-encode call sites through the capable codecs so the wire
actually carries rich text, and prove convergence:
- **Cloud:** replace the direct `_text_to_adf` (= `adf.text_to_adf`) encode at
  `adapters/jira/acli.py:205` and `acli_cli_ops.py:369` with the `AdfCodec`
  wire op, and the direct `adf.normalize_description`/`adf.fit_text_to_adf_limit`
  compare sites at `outbound_fields.py:564` and `inbound_differ.py:210` with the
  codec's `normalize_outbound`/`fit_outbound`. Each already-synced description
  re-emits **exactly once** (the `outbound_fields.py:564` once-only re-emit
  mechanism) to upgrade to rich ADF, then converges.
- **DC:** apply `WikiTextCodec.to_wire` on the description reaching
  `update_issue` — the shared composition at `outbound_mapper.py:77` and the
  CREATE path at `backend.py:70` — so `issue.update(fields=…)` receives rendered
  wiki, while the compare still uses `normalize_outbound`.
- **Rollback:** the cutover is gated behind a single switch (config/flag) that
  restores the plain/identity path for that client without reverting the codec
  capability, so a bad rollout is one revert, not a code rewrite.

## Approach (echo-safety + concurrency)
Drive body sync from a three-way state — `baseline` (last-synced Jira canonical
form), `local` (rebar body), `remote` (current Jira value) — each normalized
through the **existing codec `normalize_outbound`** (compare-only) before diffing.
Outbound fires only when `local` differs from `baseline` (rebar-originated
change); a value equal to `baseline` is our own echo and is skipped. **The
baseline is the value OBSERVED AFTER push** — after pushing a changed field, GET
it back and store Jira's canonicalized form as the new baseline (one extra GET,
only on change) — so a benign Jira re-canonicalization is never mistaken for a
human edit. When both `local` and `remote` diverged from `baseline` (concurrent
edit), apply last-write-wins to pick the winner but always emit a detectable
conflict signal so nothing is silently lost. For the rich layer, store a
change-gated `rich_sha = sha256(rendered_wire)[:16]` (8 bytes) **inline** in the
binding (proven 0.07 KB/version stable, identical to the baseline profile; a
per-pass timestamp was proven to reproduce 0303's 12.62 KB anti-pattern) so a
re-render is only pushed when the wire actually changed. The compare stays
comparison-only and never writes back.

## Scope
- `adapters/jira/acli.py` (`:205`), `adapters/jira/acli_cli_ops.py` (`:369`),
  `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py` (`:564`), `inbound_differ.py` (`:210`) —
  Cloud live cutover through `AdfCodec` (gated).
- `adapters/jira_family/outbound_mapper.py` (`:77`),
  `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` (`:70`) — DC live cutover applying
  `to_wire` to the wire (gated).
- `binding_store.py` — inline change-gated `rich_sha` beside the existing baseline
  (`_BASELINE_FIELDS`); observed-after-push baseline update.
- the existing description differ / compare path — three-way baseline diff + LWW
  arbitration, reusing the codec `normalize_outbound` (NOT a new `norm()`, NOT
  changing the shared plain-text `inbound_fields.normalize_rich_text`).
- `tests/` — cutover, convergence, echo, conflict, and no-churn tests.

## Testing
- **Cloud convergence:** after the cutover, a converted ADF description posts once,
  and a second reconcile pass emits **zero** description updates (`test_cloud_cutover_converges`).
- **DC convergence:** a rendered-wiki description posts once and a second pass
  emits zero description updates (`test_dc_cutover_converges`).
- Self-echo: a rebar-originated body change propagates exactly once and a second
  pass pushes nothing (0 echo-back).
- Concurrent: both sides edit the same body; the pass records a conflict and
  applies LWW without discarding the loser silently (799/799-detected invariant).
- No-churn: a pass with no body change updates 0 `rich_sha` entries and writes no
  timestamp; asserted by the git-delta cost harness (≤0.07 KB/version stable).
- Rollback: with the cutover flag off, the wire reverts to the plain/identity
  encode for that client (`test_cutover_rollback_restores_plain`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] After the Cloud cutover, a converted ADF description posts once and a second
  reconcile pass emits zero description updates; verified by
  `test_cloud_cutover_converges`.
- [ ] After the DC cutover, `issue.update(fields=…)` receives rendered wiki (not
  raw Markdown) and a second pass emits zero description updates; verified by
  `test_dc_cutover_converges`.
- [ ] The three-way diff reuses the codec `normalize_outbound` for the compare and
  adds no parallel normalizer; verified by `test_echo_uses_codec_normalize`.
- [ ] Outbound fires only on a rebar-originated change and the baseline stored is
  the value observed after push; verified by `test_echo_observed_after_push` (a
  benign Jira re-canonicalization does not re-sync).
- [ ] A concurrent both-sides edit is detected and flagged under LWW with the
  losing side never silently destroyed; verified by
  `test_concurrent_conflict_detected` (799/799 over the corpus sample).
- [ ] The rich layer stores a change-gated inline 8-byte `rich_sha` and no
  per-pass timestamp, changing 0 entries on a no-op pass; verified by the
  git-delta cost harness reproducing the ≤0.07 KB/version stable profile.
- [ ] The cutover is flag-gated and reverts to the plain/identity wire when off;
  verified by `test_cutover_rollback_restores_plain`.
